content.title: About
content.content: Dried apricots are the fruit of the apricot tree (Prunus armeniaca) that have been dehydrated to reduce moisture. They have a sweet‑tart flavor and a soft, slightly chewy texture. Dried apricots are widely used in cooking, baking, muesli, and as a convenient snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried apricots are rich in beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
In ancient cultures the apricot symbolized longevity and abundance.
They are a staple ingredient in many Mediterranean and Middle Eastern dishes.
When properly stored, dried apricots can keep for up to a year.
Apricots belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to peaches and plums.

items.title: High in vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene in apricots converts to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart health.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Iron is essential for hemoglobin formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Dried apricots have a high natural sugar level, so they should be eaten in moderation, especially by people with diabetes.

items.title: Sulfites
items.content: Sulfites are sometimes added to extend shelf life and may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Food allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to apricots.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The natural acidity can irritate the stomach lining if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried apricots can be enjoyed as a snack, added to muesli, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used to make compotes and sauces. Soaking them in water rehydrates the fruit and softens the texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried apricots in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator. Discard any apricots that show mold, off‑odors, or discoloration.
